title: The Street with Three Names
title_ja: 三つの名前を持つ通り
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の教材例。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: An imaginary town has a street whose name has changed several times during the past century.
sentences.ja: 架空の町には過去一世紀に数回名前が変わった通りがある。

sentences.en: A group of students investigating local history discovers three different names on maps produced during different periods.
sentences.ja: 地域史を調べる生徒たちは異なる時期の地図に三つの名前を見つける。

sentences.en: The current name appears on all modern signs, but older residents sometimes use an earlier name when describing their daily journeys.
sentences.ja: 現在の名称は現代の標識全てにあるが高齢の住民は日々の移動を語るとき以前の名称を使うことがある。

sentences.en: The students initially regard this difference as a simple problem of vocabulary rather than a subject worthy of historical investigation.
sentences.ja: 当初は歴史調査に値する題材でなく単なる語彙の問題と見なした。

sentences.en: A teacher encourages them to examine the circumstances surrounding each change instead of merely arranging the names in chronological order.
sentences.ja: 教師は単に時系列に並べず各変更を取り巻く事情を調べるよう促す。

sentences.en: They discover that one name referred to a market that no longer exists, while another was introduced during a period of administrative reorganization.
sentences.ja: 一つは現存しない市場を指し別の名は行政再編期に導入されたと分かる。

sentences.en: The available documents describe the official reasons for the changes but contain limited information about how residents reacted to them.
sentences.ja: 資料には公式の変更理由があるが住民の反応については限られた情報しかない。

sentences.en: The group therefore avoids assuming that every name became widely accepted as soon as it appeared on a government map.
sentences.ja: そこで政府の地図に載るとすぐ全名称が広く受け入れられたとは想定しない。

sentences.en: The students compare fictional interviews with residents from several different generations.
sentences.ja: 複数世代の住民との架空のインタビューを比較する。

sentences.en: Some speakers associate an earlier name with a particular occupation or gathering place, whereas others remember it simply as the address of their childhood home.
sentences.ja: 以前の名前を特定の職業や集会場所と結びつける人もいれば幼少期の家の住所として覚えている人もいる。

sentences.en: They recognize that personal recollections may reveal how a name acquired significance without establishing the precise date on which it officially changed.
sentences.ja: 個人の記憶は名前が意味を得た経緯を示しても公式変更日を確定しないと認識する。

sentences.en: Rather than selecting one account as the definitive version, the students distinguish the types of information supported by each source.
sentences.ja: 一つの記述を決定版とせず各資料が支える情報の種類を区別する。

sentences.en: For their exhibition, the group prepares a series of maps accompanied by a timeline and short explanations of the available evidence.
sentences.ja: 展示に向け年表と根拠の短い説明を添えた地図一式を用意する。

sentences.en: They indicate uncertain dates explicitly and identify recollections as memories rather than presenting them as independently verified events.
sentences.ja: 不確かな日付を明示し記憶を独立確認済みの出来事として提示しない。

sentences.en: A separate section discusses how residents may continue using a familiar expression even after official terminology has been replaced.
sentences.ja: 公式用語が置き換わっても住民が慣れた表現を使い続ける場合を別欄で論じる。

sentences.en: The exhibition thus connects changes in administrative records with the less easily documented experiences of people who lived through them.
sentences.ja: 展示は行政記録の変化とそれを経験した人々の記録しにくい体験を結びつける。

sentences.en: A street name may function as a practical tool for identifying a location, yet it can also preserve associations with activities that once took place there.
sentences.ja: 通り名は場所特定の実用道具だがかつての活動とのつながりも保存し得る。

sentences.en: The disappearance of a name from a map does not necessarily imply that its significance has disappeared from local memory.
sentences.ja: 地図から名前が消えても地域の記憶から意味が消えたとは限らない。

sentences.en: Historical inquiry becomes richer when researchers examine the relationship between official changes and the different ways in which people experience them.
sentences.ja: 公式変化と人々の経験の仕方の関係を調べると歴史研究は豊かになる。

sentences.en: In this case, the three names provide starting points for investigating the town's past rather than three competing answers to a single question.
sentences.ja: この場合三つの名称は一つの問いへの競合回答でなく町の過去を調べる出発点になる。

questions.prompt: Why was their first interpretation limited?
options: They already knew every change's cause.
They saw names as vocabulary rather than historical evidence.
questions.explanation_ja: 語彙の違いだけと見た。

questions.prompt: What did one earlier name refer to?
options: A market that no longer exists.
Official maps do not show every resident's reaction.
Residents associated names with different experiences.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish personal memories from official dates?
options: The dates are irrelevant to history.

questions.prompt: How did students present uncertain information?
options: They claimed all events were verified.
They identified uncertain dates and labeled recollections.

questions.prompt: Why include continuing use of older expressions?
options: All residents must follow current maps.
Official changes may differ from lived language practices.
Older names are legally invalid everywhere.
questions.explanation_ja: 公式と生活上の使用の差。

options: All historical maps contain identical information.
Street names connect official history with diverse lived experiences.
